payload.statement:
# HOL Council — ch21 Glossary

Chapter under review: ch21 (quarto-book/chapters/21-glossary.qmd), "Glossary", 201 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (21-glossary.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value.

The glossary's promise (21-glossary.qmd:11): "Every mechanical term used in
this book, defined in one place." The core audit tests:
  (a) ACCURACY — every definition must match the authoritative chapter. The
      glossary is a SUMMARY, never the source of a rule: it must not invent
      mechanics, reference rules/abilities that exist nowhere else in the
      book, or contradict the chapter it summarizes. A definition that
      disagrees with its source chapter is a defect, not a new ruling.
  (b) COMPLETENESS — mechanical terms the book actually uses as vocabulary
      should be present. Missing entries are defects when the term is load-
      bearing across multiple chapters (e.g. short/long rest, Recharge,
      conditions that appear in ch13's table). Judgement is allowed: not
      every noun needs an entry; the promise is the yardstick.
  (c) CONVENTION — zero em-dashes, no stale vocabulary ("chain" is DEAD:
      ch10/11/12 use the growing-card model, "There are no spell chains"
      per the glossary itself at 21-glossary.qmd:171), en-dash for prose
      ranges (ch19: "3–4 hours"), flat damage budgets.

Cross-chapter checks use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not
this chapter:
  creation = ch02 (HP 10 + Fortitude + Knowledge at L1; HP/level +Fortitude
    min 1; Background DP 8 + Knowledge + Fortitude; "Level 0" is the
    background phase)
  ancestries/cultures = ch04 (Lucky = add one Boon to any roll once per
    session; Versatile +1 DP at Level 0; culture grants +1 skill bonus and
    two specific Disciplines or one free Discipline)
  classes = ch05 (nine classes: Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd,
    Intellect, Odd, Leader, Unbalanced, Shadow; Eccentric Spellcasting at
    ch05:250; starting kits carry arcane focus / holy symbol / focus pouch)
  core resolution = ch06 (Boon = 4d6 keep highest 3; Bane = 4d6 keep lowest
    3; success tiers Weak 1-8 / Standard 9-14 / Strong 15-18+; difficulty
    Trivial +4 ... Nearly Impossible -6; Critical = three natural 6s, ~1 in
    216)
  skills = ch07 (skill bonus +1 Novice / +2 Adept / +3 Master; difficulty
    modifiers Trivial +4 / Easy +2 / Standard +0 / Hard -2 / Nearly
    Impossible -6; a "check" = 3d6 + attribute + skill + difficulty)
  disciplines = ch08 (23 disciplines in 9 categories; rank 1-3; Novice 1 /
    Adept 2 / Master 3; attribute-scaled damage formula at ch08:195: "base
    is budget − 3 (Novice 1/2/3, Adept 3/6/9, Master 6/12/18), plus the
    card's stated attribute, minimum 1 damage; melee weapons add Brawn
    (Finesse weapons use Agility); Missile weapons and ammunition are flat")
  talents/abilities = ch09 (Tough +2/+4/+6 max HP; Fortune's Favor Novice =
    once per session reroll one natural 1, 2, or 3; Basic Archery/Basic
    Thrown are flat 1/2/3 with no attribute; Throw = +1 damage tier)
  magic = ch10 (concentration: "You can only maintain one concentration
    spell at a time. If you take damage while concentrating, make a
    Fortitude check to hold the spell together" — NO talent grants a second
    concentration anywhere in ch09/ch10/ch11/ch12)
  combat = ch13 (21-row condition table incl. Dazzled and Petrified; 13
    damage types: Physical Slashing/Piercing/Bludgeoning, Elemental
    Fire/Cold/Lightning/Acid/Poison/Thunder, Magical Force/Radiant/Necrotic/
    Psychic; Surprised = acts first in the opening round + −2 on first
    roll; Cover half −1 / three-quarters −3 / full cannot be targeted;
    Initiative 3d6 + Agility; Morale Check 3d6 no modifiers; Non-Lethal
    melee only; Dying = 3d6 no modifiers each round; wounds heal 1 per long
    rest + 1 additional with a Standard Medicine check)
  equipment = ch15 (Finesse = use Agility instead of Brawn; "Missile and
    thrown attacks are flat, no attribute added" at ch15:52)
  magic items = ch17 (found, not bought)
  advancement = ch18 (attribute increases at levels 4 and 8; ~52 career DP)
  GM guidance = ch19 (short rest = 1 hour, no default mechanical effect;
    long rest = 8 hours, HP per level, wounds, once per 24h; Recharge 5-6
    usage on Kelvath's Tidal Surge)
  bestiary = ch20 (stat blocks tag abilities "(Recharge)" — the term is
    used but NEVER defined anywhere in the book; ch20's Reading a Stat
    Block table has no frequency/Recharge row)
  reference sheets = ch22

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, vocabulary swaps, definition
                  alignment, adding a single glossary entry)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new
                  content, worked-example rewrite requiring new narrative)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; card costs
2/4/8 DP; Adept prereqs exactly 2 ranks, Master exactly 3; L3/L7 gates;
no flat +N damage riders anywhere in the book (a damage bonus must be a
budget row, a Basic-card floor of 1/2/3 + attribute, or a "+1 damage tier"
bump); one-roll principle; damage dice are dead outside the allowed
random-table exceptions; ZERO "save" vocabulary (resistance = attribute
CHECKS); leveled conditions carry a number (Burning X, Slowed X); "chain"
vocabulary is retired (growing-card model); prose ranges use en-dashes.

payload.argument: The chapter does not hold as a publishable unit on the accuracy, completeness, and convention tests. It cites a talent, Spell Weaver, that exists nowhere else in the book, contradicting the magic chapter's single-concentration rule; its attribute-scaled damage entry claims missile and thrown cards add Agility, contradicting the equipment and disciplines chapters and its own flat-damage entry; its Talent example narrows Fortune's Favor's published reroll range; and its PV entry asserts an adds-to-DR effect no authoritative chapter states, making the glossary the source of a rule it is chartered only to summarize. Load-bearing vocabulary used across chapters (short rest, long rest, Recharge) is absent, and the Condition entry omits conditions that appear in the combat chapter's table, including Dazzled and Petrified. Convention violations remain: retired chain vocabulary at two entries and a hyphenated play-time range where the GM chapter uses an en-dash. Fix classes: mechanical for removing the phantom parentheticals, correcting the missile/thrown wording, fixing the Fortune's Favor example, swapping vocabulary and dashes, and extending the Condition list; substantive for adding the missing rest and Recharge entries; design-decision for confirming PV's intended effect in an authoritative chapter so the glossary may summarize it.

payload.argument: Refute: the glossary manufactures rules the book forbids, breaking its promise of one authoritative place for every mechanical term. Two entries (lines 125 and 173) grant a second concurrent spell through a Spell Weaver talent that no chapter defines; ch10 locks concentration to one spell at a time and adds a Fortitude check on damage that the glossary drops entirely. The Attribute-Scaled Damage entry (line 47) compounds this by stating missile and thrown cards key off Agility, contradicting both the glossary's own Flat Damage entry (line 45) and the locked flat missile/thrown ruling in ch08 and ch15. A rules-lawyer reading literally gains an illegal two-spell caster and an Agility-added thrown attack. Fix: delete both Spell Weaver parentheticals and change the missile/thrown clause to flat damage with no attribute.

The magic chapter locks concentration to exactly one spell at a time and requires a Fortitude check when the caster takes damage, with no talent anywhere offering a second slot.

payload.argument: The glossary fails its one-place promise on all three audit axes. Accuracy: the Attribute-Scaled Damage entry assigns Agility to missile and thrown cards while the equipment and disciplines chapters make those attacks flat with no attribute added; the Fortune's Favor example narrows the reroll to a natural 1 although the talent chapter allows 1, 2, or 3; the Concentration entries promise a second spell through a Spell Weaver talent that appears nowhere else in the book and drop the Fortitude check the magic chapter requires when damage lands; the Surprise entry omits that ambushers move first in the opening round; the Wound entry omits the extra healing a Standard Medicine check grants; and the Attunement entry exempts Artifacts from the three-slot cap in a way the magic items chapter never states. Completeness: Dazzled and Petrified, both rows in the combat chapter's condition table, have no entries, and the load-bearing terms Recharge, short rest, and long rest are undefined even though the glossary itself uses the phrase long rest and bestiary stat blocks tag abilities with Recharge. Convention: the Ability entry still speaks of a Novice/Adept/Master chain that the same chapter declares dead, and the Session entry writes its hour range with a hyphen instead of the en-dash the GM chapter uses. Fixes: correct each broken value to the quoted authoritative text, add the missing entries, and repair the two vocabulary and typography slips.

payload.argument: The glossary breaks its own promise: several entries state mechanics that either contradict or go beyond the authoritative chapters. The Attribute-Scaled Damage entry keys missile and thrown cards to Agility, but the disciplines, equipment, and talents chapters all treat those attacks as flat (Basic Archery stays 1/2/3 at every tier); a bow user with Agility +2 would over-damage by 2 per hit under the glossary's rule. Both Concentration entries grant a second simultaneous spell through a talent called Spell Weaver that appears nowhere else in the book; the magic chapter caps concentration at one spell, full stop. The Talent entry's Fortune's Favor example only rerolls natural 1s, while the talent chapter rerolls 1, 2, or 3. The Condition entry lists twelve conditions and omits Dazzled and Petrified, both of which sit in the combat chapter's condition table. And Recharge, a tag used across the bestiary and GM guidance, has no entry at all. Fixes are glossary-local: re-key missile/thrown to flat, delete the Spell Weaver clause, correct the Fortune's Favor example, add Dazzled and Petrified to the condition coverage, and add a Recharge entry. Secondary: the Ability entry still uses the retired 'chain' wording.

payload.argument: Voice largely holds: flavor lines like the Fumble's table-groan stay in the book's brisk register, and no entry lectures or drifts into outside commentary. Consistency, however, fails in three places, so the chapter must change. First, the Ability entry still labels tier progression with the retired word 'chain' even though the same chapter's Spell Card entry, and ch10's growing-card model, disavow chains; the glossary thus contradicts its own vocabulary, and ch11 still uses 'chains' as a verb, colliding with the glossary's blanket claim. Second, the 'Spell Weaver' talent cited in both concentration entries appears nowhere else in the book, an orphan name that quietly breaks the one-place definition promise. Third, the Session entry's prose range uses a plain hyphen where ch19 renders the identical duration with an en-dash. Minimal edits restore consistency: swap 'chain' for 'progression' at line 53, resolve or delete the Spell Weaver references (also collapsing the near-duplicate Concentration and Concentration Spell entries, which restate the same rule), and en-dash the prose ranges.

evidence.claim: The Ability entry still uses the retired word 'chain' to describe the Novice/Adept/Master tier progression.
The Spell Card entry flatly states spell chains do not exist, contradicting the Ability entry's vocabulary within the same chapter.
The magic chapter defines the replacement model: each spell is a single growing card bought at one tier, deepening rather than chaining.

The authoritative concentration rule allows maintaining only one concentration spell at a time, with no talent exception.

The GM guidance chapter renders the same duration with an en-dash, the book-standard spelling for prose ranges.
The Fumble entry's flavor line matches the book's punchy register, confirming the flavor-vs-rules balance holds even as consistency fails.
The combat chapter's opening sets the same brisk register the glossary's flavor lines echo, showing no tonal drift between them.

payload.argument: Measured against its own yardstick — that every mechanical term the book uses gets its definition here, in one place — ch21 does not hold. Completeness fails on load-bearing vocabulary: short rest and long rest have no entries even though ch19 defines resting, ch13 ties wound recovery and Medicine checks to rests, ch15's bedroll and healer's kit key off rests, and ch04's Second Breakfast triggers during one; Recharge, the frequency tag on a dozen ch20 stat blocks and on ch19's sample monster, is defined nowhere in the book; and Dazzled and Petrified, both rows of ch13's condition table and both used by monsters and items, appear nowhere in the glossary, whose Condition master list names only 12 of 21 conditions. Accuracy breaks too: the Attribute-Scaled Damage entry says missile and thrown cards add Agility, contradicting the flat-damage rule in ch08 and ch15 and the chapter's own Flat Damage entry, and both Concentration entries promise a second simultaneous spell via a Spell Weaver talent that no chapter anywhere grants. Convention is also nicked: the Ability entry keeps the retired 'chain' wording the chapter itself disavows, and the Session entry writes a hyphen where prose ranges take en-dashes. Structure and cross-references, by contrast, hold: all three @sec anchors resolve, heading hierarchy is consistent, the illustration caption pattern matches sibling chapters, and there are no em-dashes. The chapter is not publishable as written; the fix is a scoped revision — add the missing entries (short rest, long rest, Recharge, Dazzled, Petrified, and ideally a damage-type list), correct the missile/thrown and Spell Weaver definitions, retire the chain wording, and switch the hyphen to an en-dash.

evidence.claim: No entries define short or long rests; the only occurrence of 'long rest' sits inside the Wound entry (21-glossary.qmd:157), while ch19 defines resting, ch13 keys wound recovery and Medicine checks to rests, and ch15/ch04 gear and culture abilities depend on the terms.

Stat blocks tag monster abilities with 'Recharge' (20-bestiary.qmd:64, :104, :112, :142, :164-168, :192, :206, :236, :246, :260, :272), and ch19 uses 'Recharge 5-6' on its sample monster (19-gm-guidance.qmd:306), yet the tag is defined nowhere in the book and the glossary omits it.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Web (Recharge): Ranged attack that Restrains target

evidence.claim: The 21-row condition table includes Dazzled and Petrified (13-combat.qmd:175, :183), both of which are used elsewhere — ch17's magic item inflicts Dazzled (17-magic-items.qmd:257) and ch20's basilisk petrifies (20-bestiary.qmd:140) — but neither term appears anywhere in the glossary.

The Condition entry's master list (21-glossary.qmd:127) names only 12 of the 21 conditions in ch13's table; the seven leveled conditions have dedicated entries just below but are left off the list, and Dazzled and Petrified are absent from both the list and the chapter.

The Attribute-Scaled Damage entry (21-glossary.qmd:47) asserts missile and thrown cards add Agility, which contradicts the flat-damage rule in the equipment and disciplines chapters and the glossary's own Flat Damage entry (21-glossary.qmd:45).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: missile and thrown cards add Agility

evidence.claim: The equipment chapter is explicit that missile and thrown attacks are flat with no attribute added (15-equipment.qmd:52), and ch08 states missile weapons and ammunition are flat (08-disciplines.qmd:195) — the rule the glossary's claim would break.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Missile and thrown attacks are flat, no attribute added

evidence.claim: Both Concentration entries (21-glossary.qmd:125, :173) promise a second simultaneous spell via a Spell Weaver talent, but the name appears nowhere in ch09, ch10, ch11, or ch12 — the reference is invented and the mechanic it grants has no source chapter.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: two with the Spell Weaver talent

evidence.claim: The magic chapter permits only one concentration spell at a time and calls for a Fortitude check to hold it when damage is taken (10-magic-system.qmd:99); no talent in the book grants a second slot.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: You can only maintain one concentration spell at a time

evidence.claim: The Ability entry (21-glossary.qmd:53) still uses the retired 'chain' wording even though the chapter itself later states there are no spell chains (21-glossary.qmd:171).
The Session entry (21-glossary.qmd:197) writes '3-4 hours' with a hyphen, against the book convention of en-dashes in prose ranges, which ch19 follows for the same span.

Within sections the entries are grouped topically rather than alphabetically, with slips such as Boon before Bane (21-glossary.qmd:27, :29) and Eccentric Spellcasting after Signature Ability (21-glossary.qmd:79, :81), slowing lookup in a chapter the promise directs readers to use as a first stop.

The Protection Value entry's 'Adds to DR' (21-glossary.qmd:119) is the only statement of PV's mechanical effect anywhere in the book — ch05 and ch02 only say the signature abilities add +1 to PV, and ch22 calls it a defensive stance bonus — so the summary stands in as the source of a rule rather than summarizing one.
The Talent example understates Fortune's Favor (21-glossary.qmd:85): ch09's Novice tier rerolls a natural 1, 2, or 3 (09-talents-abilities.qmd:29), not only a natural 1.

Structure and cross-references hold: all three @sec anchors resolve (damage budget in ch08, classes in ch05, combat in ch13), headings are consistently two-level with bolded entries, the illustration caption pattern matches sibling chapters, zero em-dashes appear, and the chapter sits directly before ch22.

payload.argument: The glossary's page presentation largely holds: the em-dash prohibition is respected across all 201 lines, the heading scheme is a flat set of five second-level sections with nothing skipped and entries styled uniformly as bold-term paragraphs, each section starts after a page break so no header can dangle at a page bottom, the opening art-and-caption block reproduces the sibling chapters' pattern exactly, all @sec- references point at real anchors, and no tables exist to overflow. The refute rests on typography conventions that are in force: the Session entry renders its play-time range with an ASCII hyphen where the GM chapter uses an en-dash for the same phrase, the Bell Curve entry does the same for its cluster range, and negative values mix a Unicode minus with ASCII hyphens inside the chapter. Fixes are character-level and contained: two en-dash substitutions plus one glyph-unification pass; no reflow, re-pagination, or structural change is needed.

evidence.claim: A full-file search for the em-dash character returns zero hits, so the no-em-dash rule holds for this chapter.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Every mechanical term used in this book, defined in one place.

evidence.claim: The Session entry states the play-time range with a plain hyphen, unlike the en-dash the identical phrase carries in the GM guidance chapter.
The GM guidance chapter writes the same play-time phrase with an en-dash, which is the prose-range convention the glossary entry departs from.

Negative values inside the chapter use two distinct glyphs: one Unicode minus in the Attribute-Scaled Damage entry, plain hyphens in four other entries, so number formatting is internally inconsistent.

The heading scheme is a clean flat run of five second-level sections with no third level and no skipped levels; entries are uniform bold-term-plus-definition paragraphs, and every section begins after a page break, so no heading can sit orphaned at a page bottom.

The opening block (illustration with width attribute, italic caption line, page break, one-paragraph intro, page break) reproduces the sibling chapters' opening pattern, making it a book-wide convention rather than a local flaw.
All three cross-reference anchors used here resolve to real targets elsewhere in the book, so the PDF should not show broken links.
In the combat section the conditional-effect entries open with Burning before Asleep and place Lift after Trip, both breaks from alphabetical order in a chapter whose promise is quick look-up.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Burning X:** Takes X fire damage per round.

payload.rationale: All seven voters refuted t-01 unanimously (f-001..f-007), quorum 4, reject_quorum 4: the glossary fails its own promise ('Every mechanical term used in this book, defined in one place') and twice invents rules that contradict the authoritative chapters — the phantom 'Spell Weaver' talent (no hit anywhere in ch09-12; ch10:99 allows one concentration spell) and the missile/thrown +Agility damage claim (contradicts ch08:195 and ch15:52, both of which state missile/thrown are flat; ch09 Basic Archery/Basic Thrown are flat 1/2/3). The completeness gap is real: Dazzled and Petrified are in ch13's 21-row condition table but absent from the glossary's Condition list, and Recharge and the rests (short/long) are load-bearing terms used across ch19/ch20 with no definition anywhere. The remaining defects are vocabulary (retired 'chain' wording), precision (Fortune's Favor, Wound, Surprise, Concentration), and typography (en-dash prose ranges).
